docs.title: PyPSA Validation Processing
docs.text: This package processes PyPSA network results into IAMC-formatted variables for validation against the Eurostat Energy Balance, as part of the PyPSA-AT project.

docs.title: Scenario Explorer
docs.text:
Processed output from this package is intended for submission to the PyPSA-AT Scenario Explorer. Submitting to the Explorer requires registering a user account on the site.

Keep the following in mind when preparing a submission:

  • Model name: the Explorer currently only accepts model names starting with "Pypsa-AT v1.0" as this is the model registered. The model_name value in your config must exactly match one of the models defined in the pypsa-at-dev-workflow mappings file — set it accordingly in config.default.yaml (or your own config) before running the workflow.
  • Submission time: large files can take a while to process; you will be notified by e-mail once the submission succeeds.
  • Output format: this package's exported Excel files are already formatted to fit Explorer submission requirements. A few config flags directly affect whether a submission validates:
  • convert_units — converts PyPSA units to the IAMC-valid units expected by the Explorer.
  • map_country_codes_to_names — controls whether output regions use country codes (AT) or full names (Austria); make sure this matches what the Explorer expects for your submission.
  • aggregation_level — controls whether output rows are aggregated to country or kept at region granularity.
  • Common definitions: The common definitions of variables and regions used in this processing step must be identical to the common definitions used for the pypsa-at-dev-workflow. This is currently enshured for by default.

docs.title: Project Context
docs.text: This package computes IAMC variables from PyPSA network results and is part of the PyPSA-AT project (PyPSA-AT – a nationally tailored, fully sector-coupled energy system model for Austria). The initial set of IAMC variables is defined in energy-scenarios-at-workflow.

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text:
• Python ≥ 3.11 (pixi.toml is authoritative); type hints are required in all function signatures.
  • Docstrings follow the NumPy style (no type hints in docstrings — they belong in the signature).
  • Format code with pixi run black . before opening a pull request.

docs.title: Function Architecture
docs.text:
• Statistics functions in pypsa_validation_processing/statistics_functions.py are independent: each corresponds to one IAMC variable and must never import or call another statistics function.
  • Statistics functions may only rely on helpers in pypsa_validation_processing/utils.py for shared logic.
  • Helpers in utils.py may call other utils.py helpers, but must never call statistics functions.

docs.title: Naming convention
docs.text:
Function names follow the IAMC variable name with these substitutions:

  • Each | (pipe / hierarchy separator) is replaced by __ (double underscore).
  • Spaces are replaced by _ (single underscore).
  • Other special characters are removed.
IAMC Variable Function Name Final Energy [by Carrier]\|Electricity Final_Energy_by_Carrier__Electricity Final Energy [by Sector]\|Transportation Final_Energy_by_Sector__Transportation

docs.title: Fixed signature
docs.text:
Every statistics function takes n: pypsa.Network (one network / investment year) and aggregate_per_year: bool = True:

def <function_name>(
    n: pypsa.Network,
    aggregate_per_year: bool = True,
    <config: dict>,
) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame:
    ...

Additional optional parameters can be added when a variable needs them, e.g. config: dict or energy_totals: pd.DataFrame. All class-Variables can be used as parameters. Additional parameters are identified automatically when processing the statistics-function.

docs.title: Return format
docs.text:
• aggregate_per_year=True → return a pandas.Series.
  • aggregate_per_year=False → return a pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.
  • In both cases, the index must include at least the location and unit levels.

docs.title: Mapping file
docs.text: configs/mapping.default.yaml maps each IAMC variable name to its corresponding function name in statistics_functions.py. At runtime, Network_Processor looks up the function for each defined variable via this mapping. Variables without a mapping entry are silently skipped.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
• Use the standard library logging module.
  • Each module gets its own logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) near the top of the file.
  • pypsa_validation_processing/workflow.py::main() configures logging once via utils.setup_logging(); statistics functions and helpers must not call it themselves.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Tests live only in tests/ — see the testing README.
  • Write unit tests that test small, isolated logic.
  • Every test for a function in statistics_functions.py must assert the output format: a pandas.Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or a pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns (aggregate_per_year=False), with a MultiIndex containing at least location and unit (it can include more levels).

docs.title: Contribution Workflow
docs.text:
1. Open a new issue and select the "New Variable Statistics" issue template (for new IAMC variables) or describe the change you're proposing.
  2. Create a branch linked to the issue.
  3. Implement the change, following the conventions above.
  4. Add or update tests in tests/.
  5. Make sure pixi run test and pixi run workflow_test pass, and that there is no leftover debug code, commented-out blocks, or TODO stubs.
  6. Merge the newest main into your feature branch.
  7. Open a pull request and assign @maxnutz as reviewer.

docs.title: Network_Processor
docs.text:
Processes a PyPSA NetworkCollection against IAMC variable definitions.

Reads variable definitions from a definitions folder, executes the corresponding statistics functions to extract values from a given PyPSA NetworkCollection, and returns the results as a pyam.IamDataFrame.

Outputs are converted to the units of common definitions, set in the definitions variable in definitions_path via :meth:pyam.IamDataFrame.convert_unit if convert_units is True in config.

If definitions_path is set to False (as a YAML bool or the string "False"/"false"), definitions are disabled entirely: every variable in the mapping file (mapping_path) is evaluated regardless of whether it has a definitions-folder entry, and unit conversion is skipped.

docs.title: calculate_variables_values() -> None
docs.text:
Calculate values for all defined variables.

Iterates over all variables in self.dsd (or, when self.use_definitions is False, over every variable in self.functions_dict), calls :meth:_execute_function_for_variable for each one, and assembles the results.

When self.aggregate_per_year is True (default), assembles a single :class:pyam.IamDataFrame with one column per investment year and stores it in self.dsd_with_values.

When self.aggregate_per_year is False, stores a list[tuple[int, pyam.IamDataFrame]] in self.dsd_with_values, one entry per investment year. Each :class:pyam.IamDataFrame contains the full time-series for that year.

Applies aggregation based on self.aggregation_level config.

Raises:

Type Description RuntimeError

If no variable produced values for any network.

docs.title: read_definitions() -> nomenclature.DataStructureDefinition
docs.text:
Read IAMC variable definitions from the definitions folder.

Populates dsd with a :class:nomenclature.DataStructureDefinition built from self.definitions_path and returns it.

Returns:

Type Description DataStructureDefinition

The loaded data structure definition.

docs.title: structure_pyam_from_pandas(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pyam.IamDataFrame
docs.text:
Creates a pyam.IamDataFrame from a pandas DataFrame.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default df DataFrame

DataFrame with IAMC variables as columns and years as index.

required

Returns:

Type Description IamDataFrame

A pyam.IamDataFrame with IAMC variables as columns and years as index.

Notes

When aggregation_level="country", region labels are country codes by default. If map_country_codes_to_names is True in config, country codes are mapped to full names via :data:REGION_MAPPING. For country="all", the country column in df (populated by :meth:_aggregate_to_country) is used as the region dimension, one row per country. When aggregation_level="region", the location column in df is used directly.

docs.title: write_output_to_xlsx() -> Path
docs.text:
Write the computed IAMC data to an Excel file (or files) (C10).

<name> is <model>_<scenario>_<level>[_<country>] (:meth:_output_name), <level> the aggregation_level.

  • When aggregate_per_year=True: writes a single file <self.path_dsd_with_values>/PYPSA_<name>.xlsx.
  • When aggregate_per_year=False: creates a sub-folder <self.path_dsd_with_values>/PYPSA_timeseries_<name>/ and writes one file per investment year named PYPSA_<name>_<year>.xlsx.

The output directory is created if it does not exist.

Returns:

Type Description Path

Path to the written file (aggregate_per_year=True) or to the folder containing all per-year files (aggregate_per_year=False).

Raises:

Type Description RuntimeError

If :meth:calculate_variables_values has not been called yet.

docs.title: format_timestamps(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Normalize timestamp-like columns to tz-aware objects or formatted integers in UTC+00:00.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default df DataFrame

DataFrame whose columns may contain year strings, date strings, or timestamp-like values.

required

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

The same DataFrame with columns converted to Python datetime objects localized to +00:00 where possible for timeseries. For yearly aggregated data, columns are converted to integers.

Notes

Columns that cannot be parsed as timestamps are left unchanged. Values that can be parsed but cannot be localized are replaced with pd.NaT and reported via logger warnings. Yearly aggregated data is identified by all column labels being 4-digit year strings only. In this case, the columns are converted to integers. For non-aggregated data, columns are converted to Python datetime objects localized to UTC+00:00.

docs.title: statistics_functions
docs.text:
Statistics functions for PyPSA validation processing.

Each function in this module corresponds to one IAMC variable and extracts the relevant value from a given PyPSA Network. The functions are looked up by name via the mapping defined in configs/mapping.default.yaml.

For statistics-functions, the fixed input is n = pypsa.Network (one network / investment year) and aggregate_per_year: bool = True to switch between yearly aggregation and full snapshot time series.

If a variable-specific function needs additional settings, optional function parameters can be added. Currently, these include config and energy totals. The functions signature is identified automatically.

Each function returns a :class:pandas.Series with MultiIndex, holding at least the indexes location and unit (for aggregate_per_year = True) or a :class:pandas.DataFrame with MultiIndex and snapshots as columns (for aggregate_per_year = False).

Region Level: Regions in the returned Series correspond to the network's bus regions (e.g., "AT1", "AT2", "AT3" for pypsa-at). The postprocessing layer in Network_Processor handles aggregation to country level or keeps regions based on the aggregation_level configuration by the name of the entries of location. All regions starting with the given country-entry are grouped together.

docs.title: Final_Energy_by_Carrier__Electricity(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract Final Energy [by Carrier]|Electricity from a PyPSA Network.

Sum of the electricity withdrawn from low voltage buses by the sector consumers (agriculture, residential and commercial incl. decentral heat pumps and resistive heaters, BEV charger, industry electricity), minus the V2G feed-in to low voltage (per snapshot, not clipped), plus the DAC withdrawal from AC buses. Distribution grid, storage chargers and district-heat suppliers (urban central …) are excluded.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit and every location of the network (C6.13).

Notes

home battery charger (withdrawal) and home battery discharger (supply) are both excluded. Measured on the networks in resources/ (20261020_carbon_accounting_run, AT_KN2040, AT_KN2040_1H, electricity_network_0p3): the home battery stores are cyclic, so charger minus discharger equals the round-trip loss, charger · (1 − η²) with η = 0.98. The largest loss is 3.05 TWh (AT_KN2040_1H 2040, 0.06 % of the low voltage withdrawal); it is not counted.

docs.title: Net_Imports__Electricity(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract net imports of electricity from a PyPSA Network.

For location l: NI(l) = Σ (−p_port) over all ports of AC Lines and DC Links at AC buses in l, i.e. the energy fed into l minus the energy withdrawn from it. Imports over a lossy branch are counted at the receiving port, exports at the sending port. Positive = net import, negative = net export. Country values follow from summing locations (C8, class flow).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit and every location of the network; locations without branches get 0.0 (C6.13).

Notes

Limitation: the losses of branches between two locations of the same country are not cross-border flows, but stay in the country sum as negative net imports. The country value is therefore its cross-border net imports minus its internal branch losses (accepted bias, spec Net_Imports__Electricity.md section 7). Branches with both ends in the same location do not exist by model design.

docs.title: Final_Energy_by_Carrier__Coal(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True, industry_non_energy_shares: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract Final Energy [by Carrier]|Coal from a PyPSA Network.

FE(l) = E(l) · (1 − κ) + E(l) · κ / 1.366 with E(l) = L[coal for industry](l) − NE_coal(l): the coal for industry Load minus its non-energy use (D5), with the coke correction (D6). Coal for power plants and CHPs is transformation, not final energy.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True industry_non_energy_shares DataFrame | None

Eurostat non-energy shares, index (country, carrier), column non_energy_share (C2.5). Without industry production data in the network, κ = 0 (Eurostat fallback, D6).

None

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit and every location of the network (C6.13).

docs.title: Final_Energy_by_Carrier__Oil(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True, energy_totals: pd.DataFrame | None = None, industry_non_energy_shares: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract Final Energy [by Carrier]|Oil from a PyPSA Network.

FE(l) = f_oil · (L[agriculture machinery oil](l) + W[oil, decentral oil boilers](l) + L[land transport oil](l) + d_aviation(c) · s_ker(l) · L[kerosene for aviation](l) + d_navigation(c) · L[shipping oil](l) + L[naphtha for industry](l) − NE_naphtha(l)): the fossil share (D2) of the oil consumed by the sectors. Boilers are located per D1, domestic shares per country (D4), non-energy use per D5. s_ker is the yearly oil-based share of the kerosene supply at l. shipping methanol is not oil. Units are returned as pypsa reports them (D7).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True energy_totals DataFrame | None

Energy totals of one year, indexed by country (C2.4), for the domestic shares of aviation and navigation (D4). Required if the network has a kerosene for aviation or shipping oil Load.

None industry_non_energy_shares DataFrame | None

Eurostat non-energy shares, index (country, carrier), column non_energy_share (C2.5). Required if the network has a naphtha for industry Load.

None

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit and every location of the network (C6.13).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a carrier other than kerosene for aviation and methanol-to-kerosene supplies a kerosene for aviation bus; if energy_totals is None and the network has a kerosene for aviation or shipping oil Load; or if industry_non_energy_shares is None and the network has a naphtha for industry Load.

docs.title: Net_Imports__Oil(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract net imports of oil from a PyPSA Network.

NI(l) = f_oil · (Σ_c W[oil, c](l) + ΔE_store(l)) − S[oil, oil refining](l): the fossil part of the oil withdrawn by Links (location per D1) and of the net withdrawal of oil Stores, minus the fossil production of the location (D2). Positive = net import. The copperplate EU, which holds the refining, is negative; the yearly sum over all locations is 0.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit and every location of the network (C6.13).

Notes

The result counts only oil the model consumes. Energy statistics (Eurostat IMP − EXP, Statistik Austria) count all net imports of oil, including oil for non-energy use and refinery own use. PyPSA-AT models neither, except naphtha for industry. So the result is lower than statistics by about non-energy use minus naphtha plus refinery own use. For AT 2024 (Eurostat), that is 65.6 − 13.7 + 23.1 ≈ 75 PJ, about 17 % of net imports. Take this into account in comparisons with statistics or other models.

docs.title: Final_Energy_by_Carrier__Natural_Gas(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True, industry_non_energy_shares: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract Final Energy [by Carrier]|Natural Gas from a PyPSA Network.

FE(l) = f_gas · (W[gas, decentral gas boilers](l) + L[gas for industry](l) − NE_gas(l)): the fossil share (D3) of the gas withdrawn by decentral boilers (location per D1) and of the energy part of the gas for industry Load (non-energy use per D5). Central boilers, CHPs, power plants and SMR are transformation, not final energy.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True industry_non_energy_shares DataFrame | None

Eurostat non-energy shares, index (country, carrier), column non_energy_share (C2.5).

None

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit and every location of the network (C6.13).

docs.title: Final_Energy_by_Carrier__District_Heat(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True, config: dict | None = None) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract Final Energy [by Carrier]|District Heat from a PyPSA Network.

Heat delivered from district heating grids to consumers, without distribution losses: FE(l) = L[urban central heat](l) / (1 + λ) + L[low-temperature heat for industry](l) + W[DAC](l), all withdrawn from urban central heat buses at l. Storage chargers and the heat vent withdraw heat but are not consumers; supplying links are not counted.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True config dict | None

Network config; λ is config["sector"]["district_heating"]["district_heating_loss"].

None

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit and every location of the network (C6.13).

Raises:

Type Description MissingInputError

If the district heating loss is missing in config.

ValueError

If a DAC Link supplies heat to an urban central heat bus, or a component with an unknown carrier withdraws from such a bus.

docs.title: Final_Energy_by_Sector__Transportation(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True, energy_totals: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract Final Energy [by Sector]|Transportation from a PyPSA Network.

FE(l) = W[low voltage, BEV charger](l) − S[low voltage, V2G](l) + L[electricity for rail](l) + L[land transport fuel cell](l) + L[land transport oil](l) + d_aviation(c) · L[kerosene for aviation](l) + d_navigation(c) · (L[shipping oil](l) + L[shipping methanol](l)). The BEV charger withdrawal already includes charging losses and is not divided by an efficiency; the V2G feed-in is subtracted per snapshot, without clipping. Units are returned as pypsa reports them (incl. land transport, D7); Network_Processor normalises them.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True energy_totals DataFrame | None

Energy totals of one year, indexed by country (C2.4), for the domestic shares of aviation and navigation (D4).

None

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit and every location of the network (C6.13).

docs.title: Final_Energy_by_Sector__Industry(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True, industry_non_energy_shares: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract Final Energy [by Sector]|Industry from a PyPSA Network.

Industry excluding non-energy use: industry electricity, low-temperature heat for industry on urban central heat buses, the industrial share of the decentral heat input (D8), solid biomass for industry and the gas, H2, naphtha and coal for industry Loads minus their non-energy use (D5); coal with the coke correction (D6). industry methanol and supply-link losses are not counted.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True industry_non_energy_shares DataFrame | None

Eurostat non-energy shares, index (country, carrier), column non_energy_share (C2.5). Required if the network has gas, naphtha or coal for industry Loads; Network_Processor skips the variable if the table is not available.

None

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit (MWh) and every location of the network (C6.13).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If industry_non_energy_shares is None and the network has a gas, naphtha or coal for industry Load.

Notes

The non-energy use NE_x(l) (feedstocks) is determined with the Eurostat fallback (D5, C2.5), because the networks do not carry industry production data for the physical method of pypsa-de yet:

  • NE_x(l) = S[c, x] · L[x for industry](l), with S the share FC_IND_NE / (FC_IND_E + FC_IND_NE) of the Eurostat energy balance (FC_NE for coal) and c the country of location l (first two characters). x maps the Loads gas, naphtha and coal for industry to the Eurostat carriers Natural Gas, Oil and Coal.
  • A country without a share gets the mean share of all countries for that carrier, with a WARNING.
  • NE_H2 = 0 (Eurostat has no hydrogen share), with a WARNING.
  • The coke correction of coal uses κ = 0 (D6), with a WARNING.

See :func:~pypsa_validation_processing.utils.non_energy_use and :func:~pypsa_validation_processing.utils.apply_coke_correction.

docs.title: Final_Energy_by_Sector__Agriculture(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract Final Energy [by Sector]|Agriculture from a PyPSA Network.

FE(l) = L[agriculture electricity](l) + L[agriculture machinery electric](l) + L[agriculture machinery oil](l) + D8_agr(l). Losses of the machinery oil supply Links are not final energy.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit (MWh) and every location of the network (C6.13).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If an agriculture heat Load sits on an urban central heat bus.

Notes

Agricultural heat is produced decentrally on the rural heat bus, so it is not reported as heat in final energy. Instead, the final energy is the input carriers of the decentral heat supply (e.g. biomass, electricity of heat pumps, CHP heat output), allocated to agriculture by its share of the rural heat demand (D8, decentral_heat_split). The agriculture heat Load itself is therefore not counted.

docs.title: Final_Energy_by_Sector__Residential_and_Commercial(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True, config: dict | None = None) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Extract Final Energy [by Sector]|Residential and Commercial.

FE(l) = Σ W[low voltage, c](l) + L[urban central heat](l) / (1 + λ) + D8_rc(l). The electricity term covers the low voltage consumers of the sector; it excludes industry, agriculture, transport (rail, road, BEV charger), storage chargers, the distribution grid, district-heat suppliers and every Link supplying a decentral heat bus, whose input enters only via the residential/commercial share of the decentral heat input (D8).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

PyPSA network to process.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), aggregate over all snapshots and return a :class:pandas.Series. If False, return a :class:pandas.DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True config dict | None

Network config; λ is config["sector"]["district_heating"]["district_heating_loss"].

None

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Series (aggregate_per_year=True) or DataFrame (aggregate_per_year=False) with MultiIndex location, unit (MWh) and every location of the network (C6.13).

Raises:

Type Description MissingInputError

If the district heating loss is missing in config.

docs.title: create_location_index_from_copperplate(raw_input: pd.Series | pd.DataFrame, usage_location_list: list, column_name: str = 'location')
docs.text:
Replace the values of level column_name of an indexed object. Default column_name to be replaced is "location" for backward compatibility.

This helper rebuilds the index of raw_input from its index frame and overwrites the column_name column with values from usage_location_list. It is mainly used when location information from a copperplate-carrier result must be mapped back to explicit regional labels.

docs.title: attribute_locations(n: pypsa.Network, flows: pd.Series | pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Attribute flows on copperplate buses to a location (D1).

pypsa.statistics already attributes a flow to the location of the bus at the evaluated port (D1.1, D1.2). This helper applies the copperplate exception: a Link flow at location EU is moved to the location of the Link's bus1 (D1.3). If bus1 is a copperplate bus as well, the flow stays at EU (D1.4). Flows of other components are not changed.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

Network the flows were evaluated on.

required flows Series | DataFrame

Result of a pypsa.statistics call whose index contains the levels component, name and location. pypsa.statistics drops the component level if components is a single string, so pass a list (e.g. components=["Link"]).

required

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Copy of flows with the location level replaced. Rows are not regrouped, so two rows may now share all index values.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the index of flows lacks one of the required levels.

docs.title: apply_domestic_share(energy_stats: pd.Series | pd.DataFrame, energy_totals: pd.DataFrame | None, kind: str) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Multiply flows by the domestic share d_k(c) of their country (D4).

d_k(c) = total domestic k / (total domestic k + total international k) with c = the first two characters of the location. The share is looked up only for rows with a non-zero value (in any snapshot); rows that are 0 everywhere stay 0 without a lookup, e.g. the pseudo-location EU.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default energy_stats Series | DataFrame

Energy statistics with a location index level; a DataFrame has snapshots as columns.

required energy_totals DataFrame | None

Energy totals of one year, indexed by country (C2.4).

required kind str

"aviation" or "navigation".

required

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

energy_stats multiplied row-wise by d_k; a denominator of 0 gives 0.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If energy_totals is None or kind is not supported.

MissingInputError

If a row with non-zero Energy statistics belongs to a country without a row in energy_totals; Network_Processor then skips the variable.

docs.title: non_energy_use(demand: pd.Series | pd.DataFrame, shares: pd.DataFrame | None, carrier: str) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Return the industrial non-energy use NE_x(l) (D5, Eurostat fallback).

NE_x(l) = S[c, x] · demand(l) with c = the first two characters of the location and S the Eurostat shares (C2.5). A country without a row for carrier gets the unweighted mean of all rows of carrier, with one WARNING per call naming the countries (none for the copperplate EU). NE_H2 is 0, with one WARNING per call. 0 ≤ S ≤ 1 is checked when the file is read; a share outside [0, 1] here (e.g. after an adaptation of the shares) is clipped to [0, 1] with one WARNING per call, so 0 ≤ NE_x(l) ≤ demand(l).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default demand Series | DataFrame

Industry demand of carrier (e.g. the gas for industry Load) with a location index level; a DataFrame has snapshots as columns.

required shares DataFrame | None

Index (country, carrier), column non_energy_share (C2.5). Read from the CSV written by the sister package eurostat-energy-balance_processing (utils.calculate_industry_non_energy_shares, written by IAMC_Creator.write_industry_non_energy_shares).

required carrier str

"Natural Gas", "Oil", "Coal" or "H2".

required

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Non-energy use with the index and columns of demand.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If carrier is not supported, or shares is None for a carrier other than "H2".

docs.title: apply_coke_correction(coal_energy: pd.Series | pd.DataFrame, kappa: float | None = None) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Apply the coke correction to the energy part of industrial coal (D6). PyPSA reports with coal for industry the coal, that goes into coke ovens, Eurostats final energy counts the coke, that comes out of them.

FE = E · (1 − κ) + E · κ / MWH_COAL_PER_MWH_COKE with E the coal for industry demand minus its non-energy use (D5).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default coal_energy Series | DataFrame

Energy part E of the industrial coal demand.

required kappa float | None

Coke share κ in [0, 1] from the physical method (C2.5). If None (default), the Eurostat fallback κ = 0 applies and one WARNING is logged.

None

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Coal final energy with the index and columns of coal_energy.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If kappa is outside [0, 1].

docs.title: decentral_heat_split(n: pypsa.Network, aggregate_per_year: bool = True) -> pd.Series | pd.DataFrame
docs.text:
Split the input to decentral heat supply between sectors (D8).

For each bus carrier b of DECENTRAL_HEAT_BUS_CARRIERS and location l: D8_x(l) = Σ_b σ_b,x(l) · I_b(l). I_b is the withdrawal of the Links that supply heat to b at their non-heat input ports (location per D1), plus the heat supplied by Generators (solar thermal) and by CHPs (Links with a further non-heat output) to b. Heat storage and heat vents are excluded. σ_b,x are yearly demand shares, applied to every snapshot.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n Network

Network to evaluate.

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True (default), return yearly values as a Series; otherwise a DataFrame with snapshots as columns.

True

Returns:

Type Description Series | DataFrame

Index levels sector (rc, agr, ind, other), location, carrier (input carrier) and unit (normalised to MWh, C6.5). Empty if no decentral heat bus is supplied.

required unit str

required aggregate_per_year bool

If True, return a :class:pandas.Series; if False, a :class:pandas.DataFrame with the snapshots of n as columns. Needed because n.statistics returns an empty pd.Series in both modes.

required

result plus one row per missing location (two rows, value and weight, if result has a quantity level, C6.12), with 0.0 (aggregate_per_year=False: in every snapshot column of n). Further index levels of result are NaN in the added rows; C8 aggregates them away.

Raises:
